items.label: 1C
items.claim: NTUH's whole-genome/exome reagent-with-instrument contract spend has risen about 14x annualized since 2020, so large Taiwanese hospitals are still adding sequencing volume.
items.detail: The Feb 2020 award (TD08E140, NTUH, sole bidder Genomics BioSci) was NT$13.988M for 2 years (Mar 2020–Feb 2022), about NT$7.0M a year. The 2024–25 award is NT$32.5M per 2 years (~NT$16.25M a year, from the exclusion list, F715), and the Feb 2026 award is NT$297M over 3 years (~NT$99M a year). That is 2.3x, then 14x, the 2020 annualized spend. This shows spend growth, not Gb. The 2020 contract may have covered only part of NTUH's work, and the 2026 contract bundles an instrument. It is a very small share of Illumina's global Gb.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC procurement via openfun API
items.why_new: The 2020 baseline award for NTUH WGS/WES reagents was not in the known list, so this gives a 6-year spend path.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Across 2019–2026, Genomics BioSci's Taiwanese public sequencing awards were mostly sole-bidder and closed at 83–96% of budget, with no sign of discounts deepening.
items.detail: Award-to-budget ratios, computed from the award notices I opened: X10704E (Taipei VGH exome, Jan 2019) 552/624 = 88.5%. X10809E (Taipei VGH WGS, Aug 2019) 1,200/1,440 = 83.3%. TD08E140 (NTUH, Feb 2020) 13,988/14,570 = 96.0%. The 2026 awards were R115092 (Taipei City Hospital exome) 600/691.2 = 86.8%, PK2600016 (NTUH NGS outsourcing) 5,724/6,360 = 90.0%, M11476V (Taipei VGH long-read) 11,300/13,662 = 82.7%, K115027 (NTUH CRC RNA-seq) 1,200/1,400 = 85.7%, and KA1150333 (Taoyuan CGP) 5,616/6,240 = 90.0%. The 2019–20 mean is 89.3% and the 2026 mean is 86.9%, so budget-to-award discounting is steady to only a few points tighter. Every award except KA1150333 had one bidder, and 2019 tenders had to run three rounds before an award. This is small-sample Taiwanese public data and mixes service and kit contracts.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC procurement via openfun API
items.why_new: This is the first 2019–20 vs 2026 award-to-budget comparison for the same vendor and buyer set.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: A Taoyuan public hospital had to re-tender its comprehensive cancer tissue and ctDNA testing outsourcing three times, and the winner was a non-sequencing intermediary.
items.detail: KA1150333 (Jun–Jul 2026) failed on 15 Jun (no bids) and 8 Jul (price-list quantity error) before a 24-line list drew two bids. The NT$5.616M award was 90% of the NT$6.24M budget and base price over 2 years. Genomics BioSci was ruled non-compliant, and the winner was Kimforest. The scale is trivial (about NT$2.8M a year, well under US$0.1M). It shows slow, fragmented, procurement-limited clinical CGP uptake at this tier of public hospital, not a volume ramp.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC procurement via openfun API
items.why_new: This is a CGP/ctDNA outsourcing tender and is not covered by the Taiwan WGS/NIPT/NextSeq items already listed.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: Taiwanese public research and hospital buyers paid contract prices close to budget in 2026 for sequencing services, so there is no 'insane discount' behaviour.
items.detail: NTUH PK2600016 (Apr 2026) was awarded at NT$5.724M against a NT$6.36M budget (90.0%) after the first round failed. The bidder's own original bid was NT$5.851M, above the NT$5.85M base price, and the award was then negotiated down 2.2%. NTUH K115027 (Aug 2026) was awarded at its base price of NT$1.2M against a NT$1.4M budget (85.7%) with one bidder. Taipei City Hospital R115092 (Jul 2026) was NT$0.6M against NT$0.691M (86.8%) with one bidder. Buyers extract roughly 10–14% off budget but face a single supplier in each case.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC procurement via openfun API
items.why_new: These are three new 2026 lump-sum awards (PK2600016, K115027, R115092) with their budget ratios.

notes: Only pages 1 and 4 of 7 were read, and each only to the first ~100K characters. The API's search records contain no award values. Every detail record I opened gave a lump-sum 'estimated quantity 1' award with no per-test unit prices, so the NT$/sample series the brief asked for cannot be built from this source. Most of the useful 2023–26 items are already in the exclusion list (e.g. M11476V, Kaohsiung VGH WGS, Taipei VGH). Pages 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 are unread. Pages 5–7 hold 2018 and earlier records that are not useful for the thesis. The job_number dedupe against the 49 S724 items was not done, as that list was not provided. The tool used was WebFetch, so there was no way to loop pages with 429 backoff.
